findings.claim: In `.topic-meta-data h5 a` (the bold poster-name link) the light and dark values are swapped. The original was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new code is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`; it should be (30%, 70%). On the default light theme the link fades from dark grey to pale grey, which is a light-theme regression in a commit scoped to dark themes. On dark themes it is dim instead of prominent.
findings.evidence:
1. All three seats ran scripts pairing every -/+ line, and each flagged this line.
2. open-code-review cites `git --no-pager diff 7554b5e3c4 d38c4d5f74 -- app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss | grep -A1 'lightness: 30%);$'`.
3. superpowers computed the light-theme colour going from #646464 (5.92:1 against white) to #bdbdbd (1.88:1), which is below WCAG AA.
4. No seat compiled the SCSS, because no Sass toolchain was available.
findings.reason: Three seats raised it independently, with diff evidence. The red repro is superpowers' python pairing script, which prints this line on the pinned patch. Fix: set the values to (30%, 70%).

verifier.reason: At app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 the patch swaps `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` for `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. `dark-light-choose` returns its first argument on light themes (common/foundation/variables.scss:46-51), so the light theme moves from 30% to 70% lightness, and this goes against the patch's own (30%, 70%) mapping for every other 30% line, such as the `.username a` change.

findings.claim: The same `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, X%), scale-color($secondary, (100-X)%))` pair is hand-copied 115 times across 32 files, for example `common/admin/admin_base.scss:385`. The 100-X rule is never written down. A single helper next to `dark-light-choose` or `dark-light-diff` (e.g. `primary-faded($pct)`) would encode it and would have made the 5 main-list errors impossible.
findings.evidence:
1. ponytail's script confirmed that the $secondary lightness is 100 minus the $primary lightness on all 115 added lines.
2. mattpocock flags the same pattern as a Duplicated Code / Shotgun Surgery smell.
3. open-code-review mentions it but explicitly declines to raise it as a finding.
findings.reason: Appendix: two seats, both advisory, and advisory findings never block. ponytail: maintainability refactor, not a defect. Would also prevent recurrence of the main-list mismatches.

findings.claim: Single-line rules have a stray space before `}` (`...)); }`) that does not match the surrounding style. superpowers also cites `desktop/topic-list.scss:39-54` and several one-liners in `desktop/topic-post.scss`.
findings.evidence: superpowers asserts it from reading the patch, without quoting a specific - line next to its + line.
findings.reason: Disproved by another seat's report. mattpocock checked whitespace on all 115 pairs and states that no tabs or trailing whitespace were added. It also states that the `{color: ...;}` brace spacing in single-line rules was already there before the patch, so it is not introduced here. Since every -/+ pair differs only in the colour expression, the spacing is pre-existing.

coverage:
Files skipped: none. All four seats report covering all 32 files. ponytail checked them by grep and perl rather than reading each file by hand.

Axes that did not run:
- The gate was not run (benchmark mode), so the review is unanchored and no finding has gate ground truth.
- There is no spec; every seat judged against the commit message.
- No Sass compiler was available to any seat, so there was no compiled-CSS or rendered check. Colour and contrast effects are reasoned; superpowers' contrast figures assume the default #222/#fff palette.
- The repo has no SCSS tests. The only red evidence is superpowers' diff-pairing repro script, which was not executed in this replay.
- Standards came from CONTRIBUTING.md only; there is no scss-lint config and no CODING_STANDARDS file.
- No seat checked the dark-theme visual quality of the 100-X mirror values.
- open-code-review worked from a partial clone without the base blobs and took the original values from the patch's - lines.
- No reviewer from another model family took a seat.
